nodes.name: Orders
nodes.summary: Every order screen: lists, details, drafts, fulfilment, payments, refunds, returns and order settings.
nodes.detail: Mounted under the /orders/ section by the router in src/orders/index.tsx. Each route renders a view component that loads its data with a generated Apollo hook (one per GraphQL document in queries.ts and mutations.ts), wires the mutations through the OrderOperations container or local hooks, and hands the results to presentational page components. After a mutation the views either refetch the OrderDetails query or read the order straight from the mutation response, then show a toast and navigate back to the order. Order details is status-aware: drafts, unconfirmed and normal orders get separate sub-views.

nodes.name: Customers
nodes.summary: Customer list with type tabs, customer details with attributes and spending overview, addresses, and customer types.
nodes.detail: Routes in src/customers/index.tsx render CustomerList, CustomerCreate, CustomerDetails and CustomerAddresses. Customer details loads through CustomerDetailsProvider, which runs the CustomerDetails query twice: once to discover which channels the customer bought in, then again scoped to the selected channel for the key figures panel. Saving updates identity fields, customer type and attribute values in one customerUpdate call after uploading any new attribute files. Customer types (src/customerTypes) define which attributes a customer carries.

nodes.name: Gift cards
nodes.summary: Gift card list and bulk actions, single and bulk issuing, the gift card details page, code resend and gift card settings.
nodes.detail: src/giftCards/index.tsx routes to the list, the settings page and one gift card. The list is driven by GiftCardListProvider (filters, sort, pagination, selection); issuing happens in dialogs that call giftCardCreate or giftCardBulkCreate and then refetch the list. The details page wraps its cards in three providers (details query, update form, dialogs) so activate, balance, customer assignment, resend and notes can each run their own mutation and refresh the same cached gift card.

nodes.name: Discounts and vouchers
nodes.summary: Promotions with rules and conditions, and vouchers with codes, catalogue scope, channel values and limits.
nodes.detail: src/discounts/index.tsx mounts promotions under the legacy /discounts/sales/ paths (list, add, details) and vouchers under /discounts/vouchers/. Promotions convert between the form's Rule and Condition models and the server's JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) predicates in src/discounts/models. Voucher details stages catalogue, country and code changes locally and sends them as several mutations on save, reporting which parts were saved.

nodes.name: Order routes and GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: The order router, web address builders, the GraphQL queries and mutations every order screen uses, and the operations container.
nodes.detail: queries.ts and mutations.ts hold gql documents; the build's code generator turns each into a typed hook in src/graphql/hooks.generated.ts (useOrderDetailsQuery, useFulfillOrderMutation and so on), which is what the views import. OrderOperations instantiates twenty-one of the mutation hooks at once for the details page. urls.ts builds every order path and keeps dialog state in the query string, so dialogs survive reloads.

nodes.name: Order section router
nodes.summary: Declares the thirteen order routes, parses query strings and sort parameters, and wraps the lists in conditional filter providers.
nodes.detail: Uses react-router Switch with the path builders from urls.ts. The order list and draft list parse the query string with asSortParams (default sort: number, descending) and sit inside ConditionalOrderFilterProvider or ConditionalDraftOrderFilterProvider, which turn the filter bar into a GraphQL where input. Refund routes are ordered so the edit paths with two identifiers match before the single-identifier ones. Both /orders/drafts/:id and /orders/:id render the same OrderDetails view.
facts: Draft details and order details share one view component
Order list default sort is by order number

nodes.name: Order web address builders
nodes.summary: Builds every order path and query string, including dialog actions, focused line and status-aware details links.
nodes.detail: Path helpers (orderPath, orderDraftPath, orderFulfillPath, orderTransactionRefundEditPath and others) join segments under /orders/; Url helpers add an encoded identifier and a stringified query. orderDetailsUrl picks the draft or normal path from the order status. OrderUrlDialog lists every dialog the details page can open through ?action=, and withOrderLineFocus or withOrderFulfillmentDialog add line and fulfilment parameters.

nodes.name: Order GraphQL queries
nodes.summary: Fifteen gql queries: order list, draft list, order details, fulfil data, refund data, transactions, metadata and order settings.
nodes.detail: Each document is compiled by the code generator into a hook. OrderList and OrderDraftList take cursor pagination, a where input from the filter bar, a search string and a sort input. OrderDetails reads the whole OrderDetails fragment plus shop settings (fulfilment auto-approve, allow unpaid, payment gateways). OrderDetailsGrantRefund feeds every refund page; OrderFulfillData and OrderFulfillSettings feed the fulfil page.

nodes.name: OrderDetails query
nodes.summary: Loads one order with the OrderDetails fragment and the shop settings the details page needs.
nodes.detail: The single source of truth for the details page: lines, fulfilments, transactions, granted refunds, events and totals all come from the OrderDetails fragment. Mutations elsewhere refetch this document (by name, OrderDetailsDocument) so every card refreshes together.

nodes.name: Order GraphQL mutations
nodes.summary: Forty gql mutations covering order edits, drafts, fulfilment, payments, transactions, refunds, returns, invoices and settings.
nodes.detail: Every document selects its errors list (for refunds including the failing lines), and most that change an order also return the OrderDetails fragment, so Apollo's cache updates the details page without a refetch. Two documents create the same granted refund: OrderGrantRefundAdd returns only the refund, OrderGrantRefundAddWithOrder also returns the order for the return page. Manual capture and manual refund both call transactionCreate with different amounts.

nodes.name: FulfillOrder mutation
nodes.summary: Creates fulfilments for chosen order lines and warehouses and returns the updated order and any stock errors.
nodes.detail: Sends orderFulfill(order, input) where input carries lines with per-warehouse stock quantities, notifyCustomer, allowStockToBeExceeded and an optional tracking number. Errors include warehouse and orderLines so the page can point at the failing line.

nodes.name: OrderGrantRefundAdd mutation
nodes.summary: Creates a granted refund (a refund draft) with amount, reason, reason reference, lines, shipping flag and target transaction.
nodes.detail: Used by the new refund page and the legacy grant refund page. Returns the granted refund identifier, which the new flow uses to navigate to the edit page where funds can be transferred.

nodes.name: Send refund for granted refund
nodes.summary: Asks the server to refund a granted refund through its payment transaction, which hands the request to the payment app.
nodes.detail: Calls transactionRequestRefundForGrantedRefund(grantedRefundId, id). If the granted refund is already tied to a transaction, the server ignores the transaction identifier sent here.

nodes.name: Transaction action request
nodes.summary: Requests charge, refund or cancel on a payment transaction, with optional amount and refund reason.
nodes.detail: The generic transaction action used by capture, cancel and manual refund. The server records a request event and forwards it to the app that owns the transaction; the outcome arrives later as success or failure events.

nodes.name: Order operations container
nodes.summary: Render-prop container that creates twenty-one order mutation hooks and passes them, with their state, to the details views.
nodes.detail: Each hook gets the matching onCompleted callback from OrderDetailsMessages. orderUpdate, orderDraftUpdate and fulfilment approve set disableErrorHandling so address and stock errors show inline instead of as global toasts. getMutationProviderData packs each [mutate, result] pair into { mutate, opts } for the children.
nodes.signature: const OrderOperations = ({ children, onDraftUpdate, ... }: OrderOperationsProps) => JSX.Element

nodes.name: Order fixtures
nodes.summary: Large sample orders, drafts and lines used by stories and tests of the order components.

nodes.name: Order feature announcements
nodes.summary: Ripple entries that announce new order features (line matrix, price breakdown, refund and return reasons, metadata) in the dashboard.
nodes.detail: Each file exports a Ripple object with an identifier, a time to live in seconds, the date added and short, contextual and global content; the shared ripples module (src/ripples) decides when to show them.

nodes.name: Order and draft lists
nodes.summary: The paginated order list and draft order list, with filter presets, search, sort, column settings and bulk draft deletion.
nodes.detail: Both lists build query variables from the conditional filter context (createOrderQueryVariables or its draft twin), the sort parameters and the paginator, then run OrderList or OrderDraftList. Results render in Glide data grids with saved column settings. Creating an order from the list first picks a channel and runs draftOrderCreate, then opens the new draft.

nodes.name: Order list view
nodes.summary: Loads the order list with filters, search, sort and pagination, and creates a draft order when staff start a new order.
nodes.detail: Reads filter values from useConditionalFilterContext and turns them into an OrderWhereInput with createOrderQueryVariables; getSortQueryVariables maps the sort parameter. Filter presets live in local storage (storageUtils). useOrderDraftCreateMutation creates a draft in the chosen channel and navigates to it; useShopLimitsQuery passes the shop's order limits to the page, which disables creation when the limit is reached.

nodes.name: Order list page
nodes.summary: Page layout for the order list: header, channel picker for new orders, filter bar, preset tabs and the data grid.

nodes.name: Order list data grid
nodes.summary: Glide data grid of orders with number, date, customer, payment, status, delivery, net, total and channel columns.
nodes.detail: datagrid.ts defines the columns and cell renderers; utils.ts derives status pills from charge, authorize and order status. Column choices persist through list settings, and row clicks open orderUrl.

nodes.name: Draft order list view
nodes.summary: Loads draft orders with filters and sort, creates new drafts and deletes selected drafts in bulk.
nodes.detail: Mirrors the order list but runs OrderDraftList; useBulkDeletion wraps draftOrderBulkDelete and handles its result in onCompleted.

nodes.name: Draft list page and grid
nodes.summary: Layout, header, data grid and bulk delete dialog for draft orders.

nodes.name: Order details
nodes.summary: The order details page: data loading and polling, status-specific sub-views, dialogs, customer and address editing, metadata and invoices.
nodes.detail: OrderDetails loads the order, canonicalises the web address to match the status, and renders OrderDetailsMessages (toasts) around OrderOperations (mutations) around one of three sub-views: OrderNormalDetails, OrderDraftDetails or OrderUnconfirmedDetails. Each sub-view renders the page and every dialog, opening them through ?action= in the address. While a payment transaction request is waiting for the payment app, useOrderTransactionPolling refetches the order every 5 seconds for up to 24 cycles.

nodes.name: Order details view
nodes.summary: Loads an order, picks the draft, unconfirmed or normal sub-view by status, and wires mutations, toasts and invoices.
nodes.detail: Confirms unconfirmed orders with orderConfirm and saves metadata through handleOrderDetailsSubmit. When an invoice request returns a pending job it queues a background INVOICE_GENERATE task. After transaction actions and manual transactions it refetches OrderDetailsDocument before showing the toast. A null order shows the not-found page; Back returns to the draft list or the order list depending on status.

nodes.name: useOrderDetails()
nodes.summary: Runs the OrderDetails query, registers it for app-triggered refreshes and turns on transaction polling.
nodes.signature: export const useOrderDetails = (id: string) => { data, loading }

nodes.name: useOrderTransactionPolling()
nodes.summary: Polls the order every 5 seconds while a transaction charge, refund or cancel request has no result yet, for at most 24 cycles.
nodes.detail: State-driven rather than click-driven: polling is on exactly while orderHasInFlightTransactionAction is true and the browser tab is visible. A rising edge resets the cycle budget; reaching 24 cycles (about two minutes of visible time) stops polling until the order goes quiet and a new request appears. Hiding the tab pauses polling and the cycle counter; showing it refetches at once. Apollo's startPolling does the fetching, a separate interval only counts cycles.
nodes.signature: useOrderTransactionPolling({ order, startPolling, stopPolling, refetch }): { isPolling: boolean }

nodes.name: handleOrderDetailsSubmit()
nodes.summary: Saves the details form: confirms an unconfirmed order first, then updates public and private metadata on the order and its lines.
nodes.detail: Stops and returns the confirm errors if orderConfirm fails. Otherwise builds a metadata update handler per metadata owner (order, lines, fulfilments) with createOrderMetadataIdSchema, runs them in parallel and shows 'Metadata updated' only when something actually changed and no errors came back.

nodes.name: Order details toasts
nodes.summary: Turns every order mutation result into a success or error toast and closes the open dialog on success.
nodes.detail: Provides one handler per mutation (cancel, void, capture, notes, draft update and finalize, fulfilment approve, cancel and tracking, invoices, transaction actions). Fulfilment approve skips the toast when every error is INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, because the dialog itself offers to exceed stock.

nodes.name: Placed order sub-view
nodes.summary: Renders a placed order's page and all its dialogs: cancel, capture, transaction action, mark as paid, void, addresses, metadata, invoices.
nodes.detail: Loads warehouses and the customer's saved addresses, computes the refund destination with getOrderRefundNavigation, and maps page callbacks to navigation (fulfil, return, refund, approve, tracking) or to OrderOperations mutations. Transaction capture and cancel go through transactionRequestAction; legacy payments use orderCapture and orderVoid.

nodes.name: Unconfirmed order sub-view
nodes.summary: Renders an unconfirmed order, which can still have lines edited and must be confirmed on save.

nodes.name: Details address canonicalisation
nodes.summary: Rewrites /orders/:id to /orders/drafts/:id (or back) once the order status is known, keeping the query string.

nodes.name: Order details page
nodes.summary: Page layout for a placed order: title, line view, fulfilments, payments summary, transactions, history, customer, invoices, metadata and save bar.
nodes.detail: Renders the order lines section (line matrix or timeline), OrderSummary and OrderTransactionsSection, history, customer and invoices, and submits metadata through the parent's onSubmit. utils.ts builds the metadata form schema keyed by owner identifier.

nodes.name: Order details view model
nodes.summary: Static rules for what the details page shows and allows: fulfil button, mark as paid, capture, void, refund, grant refund, gift card amounts.
nodes.detail: Reads the order's actions list (CAPTURE, MARK_AS_PAID, VOID, REFUND) and status. canGrantRefund needs at least one transaction or legacy payment; canSendRefund needs a granted refund; getGiftCardsAmountUsed adds up the balance drop of each gift card's USED_IN_ORDER event for this order.

nodes.name: Order customer card
nodes.summary: Shows the order's customer, email, pickup location and addresses, and lets staff change the customer or edit addresses.

nodes.name: Order address edit dialog
nodes.summary: Edits billing and shipping addresses by picking a saved customer address or typing a new one, with inline validation errors.
nodes.detail: form.tsx keeps the shipping and billing choices and the 'same as shipping' switch; the dialog returns the chosen addresses to orderUpdate or orderDraftUpdate, whose errors land on the address fields.

nodes.name: Cancel order dialogs
nodes.summary: Confirms order cancellation, or explains why an order with fulfilments cannot be cancelled.

nodes.name: Metadata dialogs
nodes.summary: Dialogs that show and edit metadata for the order, one order line or one fulfilment.
nodes.detail: The line dialog loads OrderLinesMetadata with hasManageProducts and saves through useHandleSubmit (metadata and private metadata mutations); the order and fulfilment dialogs use the shared lazy metadata dialog with OrderMetadata and OrderFulfillmentMetadata.

nodes.name: Invoice list and send
nodes.summary: Lists generated invoices, starts invoice generation and emails an invoice to the customer.

nodes.name: Order line views
nodes.summary: How order lines are shown: the line matrix with a lifecycle per line, the shipment timeline, the price waterfall and the order history.
nodes.detail: buildOrderLineLifecycle folds lines, fulfilments, granted refunds and events into one record per line (ordered, to fulfil, shipped, waiting for approval, returned, refunded). getOrderLineRollupStatus reduces that to one status pill. The view mode (matrix or timeline) is stored in list settings, migrated once from an older local storage key.

nodes.name: buildOrderLineLifecycle()
nodes.summary: Builds a per-line lifecycle from the order: quantities shipped, waiting, returned, replaced, refunded and the shipments behind them.
nodes.detail: Walks fulfilments by status (fulfilled, waiting for approval, returned, replaced, refunded) and attributes quantities to each order line, records shipment entries with warehouse and tracking number, and attaches granted refund entries with status, amount and reason. buildFulfillmentRestockWarehouseMap reads order events to find where returned stock went.

nodes.name: getOrderLineRollupStatus()
nodes.summary: Reduces a line lifecycle to one status, favouring states that need action (approval, failed refund, draft refund, partial shipment).

nodes.name: Line matrix data grid
nodes.summary: Data grid with one row per order line and columns for each lifecycle stage, with a row menu and an expandable panel per line.
nodes.detail: Row menu items come from getOrderLineRowMenuItems (product details, fulfil, return, refund) with targets from getOrderLineActionUrls; OrderLineExpandedPanel lists shipments and granted refunds for the focused line.

nodes.name: Order lines section
nodes.summary: Shows order lines either as the line matrix or as the timeline (unfulfilled lines, then one card per fulfilment), with a refund callout.

nodes.name: Line price waterfall
nodes.summary: Explains a line's price as steps from undiscounted unit price through promotions, vouchers and manual discounts to the total.
nodes.detail: buildLineWaterfall turns the line's discounts into factors with optional links (only vouchers can be linked, because order line discounts expose no promotion identifier) and absorbs residuals smaller than half a minor currency unit. LinePriceWaterfallModal renders the steps.

nodes.name: Order history timeline
nodes.summary: Shows order events as a timeline with staff notes that can be added and edited.
nodes.detail: utils.tsx maps each order event type to a message; notes go through orderNoteAdd and orderNoteUpdate.

nodes.name: useOrderDetailsViewMode()
nodes.summary: Reads and saves the matrix or timeline choice and the show-cancelled-fulfilments switch in list settings.
facts: Migrates the legacy local storage key orderDetailsViewMode once

nodes.name: Draft orders
nodes.summary: Editing a draft order: customer, addresses, lines, discounts and shipping, then finalising it into a real order.
nodes.detail: OrderDraftDetails renders OrderDraftPage with the OrderOperations mutations for lines (orderLinesCreate, orderLineUpdate, orderLineDelete), shipping, draft update, cancel and finalize. ChannelUsabilityData checks whether the channel can take an order. Finalize errors are filtered so missing-address or missing-shipping errors disappear once the data is filled in.

nodes.name: Draft order sub-view
nodes.summary: Renders a draft order with product, discount, shipping, customer and address dialogs, and finalises it with draftOrderComplete.
nodes.detail: Runs ChannelUsabilityData (products in the channel, shipping zones) and the customer's saved addresses. Adding products uses the variant search; customer change updates user and email through orderDraftUpdate.

nodes.name: getUnresolvedFinalizeErrors()
nodes.summary: Drops finalize errors for a billing address, shipping address or shipping method that the draft now has.
nodes.detail: Apollo keeps the last draftOrderComplete result until the mutation runs again, so without this filter the errors would stay on screen after staff fixed them.

nodes.name: Draft order page
nodes.summary: Page layout for a draft: lines grid, summary with shipping and discounts, customer card, history, and the Finalize save bar.

nodes.name: Draft lines grid
nodes.summary: Editable data grid of draft lines: quantity edits, line discounts, metadata and removal.

nodes.name: Add products dialog
nodes.summary: Searches products and variants available in the order's channel and adds the chosen variants as lines.

nodes.name: Order and line discount modals
nodes.summary: Adds, edits or removes a manual discount on the whole order or on one line, as a percentage or fixed amount with a reason.
nodes.detail: useDiscountForm converts the value between percentage and fixed amount using the order or line price as the base; the modals call orderDiscountAdd, orderDiscountUpdate, orderDiscountDelete, orderLineDiscountUpdate and orderLineDiscountRemove.

nodes.name: Shipping method dialog
nodes.summary: Picks a shipping method from those available for the order and saves it with orderUpdateShipping.

nodes.name: Fulfilment
nodes.summary: Fulfilling order lines from warehouses, the stock-exceeded retry, fulfilment cards, approval, cancellation, tracking numbers and warehouse changes.
nodes.detail: The fulfil page builds a formset with one row per line still to fulfil, prefilled with the full quantity and a default warehouse (the one with the biggest allocation, else the most available stock). Submitting runs orderFulfill; if every error is INSUFFICIENT_STOCK a dialog offers to resubmit with allowStockToBeExceeded. Fulfilments waiting for approval are approved from their card, which navigates to the details page with a dialog action.

nodes.name: Fulfil order view
nodes.summary: Loads fulfil data and shop settings, submits the FulfillOrder mutation and returns to the order on success.
nodes.detail: notifyCustomer is only sent when the shop auto-approves fulfilments and staff ticked 'send info'. On success it replaces the history entry with the order page and shows 'Fulfilled Items'; stock errors are left to the page's stock-exceeded dialog, other errors go to handleNestedMutationErrors.

nodes.name: Fulfil order page
nodes.summary: Formset of lines to fulfil with quantity and warehouse per line, tracking number, send-info switch and the stock-exceeded dialog.
nodes.detail: Save is enabled only when at least one quantity is above zero, no line exceeds its quantity to fulfil, every line with a quantity has a warehouse, and the shop does not forbid fulfilling unpaid orders (auto-approve on, allow unpaid off, order not paid). A lineId parameter narrows the page to one line.

nodes.name: Order data helpers
nodes.summary: Shared calculations for fulfilment, returns and refunds: lines to fulfil, warehouse stock, refundable amounts and display names.
nodes.detail: getToFulfillOrderLines keeps lines with a quantity still to fulfil; getOrderLineAvailableQuantity subtracts allocations of other orders from a warehouse's stock; getReturnSelectedProductsAmount and getReplacedProductsAmount price the lines picked on the return page; mergeRepeatedOrderLines combines fulfilment lines of the same order line.

nodes.name: getDefaultFulfillWarehouse()
nodes.summary: Picks the warehouse to prefill for a line: the allocation with the highest quantity, otherwise the stock with the most available units.

nodes.name: getOrderFulfillSubmitItems()
nodes.summary: Converts the formset into FulfillOrder lines, dropping zero quantities and rows without a warehouse.

nodes.name: Fulfilment card
nodes.summary: One fulfilment with its lines, warehouse, tracking number and approve, cancel or tracking actions.

nodes.name: Fulfilment approve, cancel and tracking dialogs
nodes.summary: Approve a waiting fulfilment (optionally notifying the customer), cancel one back to a warehouse, or change its tracking number.

nodes.name: Change warehouse dialog
nodes.summary: Lists warehouses with available stock for one line and switches the line's fulfil warehouse.

nodes.name: Payments and transactions
nodes.summary: How an order's money is shown and acted on: order value and payment summary, transaction cards with events, capture, cancel, mark as paid and manual transactions.
nodes.detail: Orders paid through the transactions model show one card per transaction with its events (request, success, failure) and action buttons; older orders show legacy payments with capture, void and refund. Buttons for an action already in flight are disabled because Saleor core does not stop duplicate requests. A spinner next to Transactions marks a request waiting for the payment app.

nodes.name: Order value and payments summary
nodes.summary: Shows subtotal, line and order discounts, shipping, taxes and total, beside authorized, charged, pending and refunded amounts.
nodes.detail: getLineDiscountsSummary groups line discounts by discount type and sums them; getUndiscountedSubtotal recomputes the subtotal before discounts. Charge and authorize badges come from the order's status enums; mark-as-paid appears when the order has no payment.

nodes.name: Transactions section
nodes.summary: Lists the refunds table, then every transaction, legacy payment and gift card used on the order, with an add-transaction button.

nodes.name: Transaction card
nodes.summary: One payment transaction: method, amounts, events with payment service provider (PSP) references, and charge, cancel or refund buttons.
nodes.detail: utils.ts maps events and actions to messages; PspReferenceLink turns the provider reference into a link when the event carries an external web address. Card, gift card and other payment methods have their own detail rows.

nodes.name: orderHasInFlightTransactionAction()
nodes.summary: True when a transaction has a charge, refund or cancel request with no success or failure event sharing its payment service provider (PSP) reference.
nodes.detail: Groups events by payment service provider (PSP) reference. It keys off events rather than pending amounts because core records the request event at once but only adds it to the pending amount after the app answers. Any success or failure resolves a request, even of another action type. transactionActionInFlight applies the same test to one action to disable its button.

nodes.name: Legacy payment and gift card cards
nodes.summary: Shows payments made through the older payments model, and gift cards spent on the order, in the transaction card layout.

nodes.name: Capture dialog
nodes.summary: Chooses how much of an authorized amount to charge, defaulting to what remains, and sends a charge request.
nodes.detail: useCaptureState computes the authorized, charged and remaining amounts and the default capture amount.

nodes.name: Payment action dialogs
nodes.summary: Confirmation dialogs for cancelling a transaction, voiding a legacy payment and marking an order as paid with a reference.

nodes.name: Manual transaction dialog
nodes.summary: Records money received outside any payment app as a manual capture transaction with amount, description and payment service provider reference.
nodes.detail: OrderManualTransactionForm keeps the amount and fields in context; submit calls transactionCreate through the CreateManualTransactionCapture document.

nodes.name: Refunds
nodes.summary: Granting refunds (drafts), sending them to the payment app, manual refunds, and the legacy refund page for orders without transactions.
nodes.detail: Orders with transactions use granted refunds: the create page saves a draft with orderGrantRefundCreate, the edit page updates it with orderGrantRefundUpdate and, once saved and the user can handle payments, transfers funds with transactionRequestRefundForGrantedRefund. A manual refund sends a refund request on one transaction directly. Orders on the legacy payments model use orderRefund or orderFulfillmentRefundProducts. The refunds table merges granted refunds and refund events into one list.

nodes.name: getOrderRefundNavigation()
nodes.summary: Sends staff to the transaction refund page when the order has transactions, otherwise to the legacy payment refund page.

nodes.name: Refund type dialog
nodes.summary: Asks whether to create a standard refund (with lines) or a manual refund; manual needs the HANDLE_PAYMENTS permission.

nodes.name: Refunds view model
nodes.summary: Merges granted refunds and manual refund events into one list sorted by date, and decides which refunds can be edited.
nodes.detail: Manual refunds have no server object, so refund events are grouped by PSP (payment service provider) reference and given the granted refund status enum. A refund can be edited only when it is not successful, not pending and not manual. getRefundState says whether any transaction allows REFUND.

nodes.name: Refunds table
nodes.summary: Table of the order's refunds with status, amount, reason, creator, per-line sub rows and edit links.

nodes.name: Create refund view
nodes.summary: Saves a new refund draft from selected lines, shipping and amount, then opens it for editing and transfer.
nodes.detail: Loads OrderDetailsGrantRefund and refund settings (the model type a refund reason must reference). Rejects an amount larger than the chosen transaction's charged amount before calling orderGrantRefundCreate. handleRefundCreateComplete navigates to the edit page on success, otherwise turns errors into per-line errors and toasts all but REQUIRED and AMOUNT_GREATER_THAN_AVAILABLE.

nodes.name: Refund create and edit handlers
nodes.summary: Shared refund helpers: completion handling, building grant refund lines and the charged-amount check.
nodes.detail: prepareRefundAddLines keeps lines with a positive quantity and maps them by position to the order's line identifiers. checkAmountExceedsChargedAmount compares the amount with the selected transaction's charged amount.

nodes.name: Edit refund and transfer view
nodes.summary: Edits a refund draft (replacing all its lines) and transfers the funds through the payment app once saved.
nodes.detail: Update sends every existing draft line as removeLines and the current selection as addLines, rejects a zero amount, and writes the returned order into the cache for OrderDetailsGrantRefund. Transfer calls transactionRequestRefundForGrantedRefund with the draft's transaction and returns to the order with 'refund request sent'.

nodes.name: Refund form page
nodes.summary: React Hook Form page with a refundable lines table, transaction tiles, reason and reason reference, shipping switch and amount summary.
nodes.detail: useRecalculateTotalAmount keeps the amount equal to the selected lines (plus shipping) whenever lines or the shipping switch change. getMaxQtyToRefund subtracts quantities already in other granted refunds.

nodes.name: getRefundFormSubmitBehavior()
nodes.summary: Makes the save bar 'Save draft' while the form is dirty or new, and 'Transfer funds' once a saved draft can be sent.
nodes.detail: Transfer appears only for an existing draft, with a clean form, a transfer handler and the HANDLE_PAYMENTS permission; otherwise the submit saves the draft.

nodes.name: Grant refund view (older page)
nodes.summary: Older grant refund page: picks lines, shipping and amount and creates a granted refund, then returns to the order.
nodes.detail: Skips the call when no line, no amount and no shipping were chosen. Lines are squashed by order line identifier before sending. OrderEditGrantRefund edits an existing granted refund with orderGrantRefundUpdate.

nodes.name: Send refund view
nodes.summary: Shows each transaction against the order's remaining granted amount, sends a refund request per transaction, or records a manual refund.
nodes.detail: useOrderSendRefund wraps transactionRequestAction with REFUND and refetches OrderDetails; the manual refund card calls transactionCreate with a refunded amount through CreateManualTransactionRefund.

nodes.name: Manual refund view
nodes.summary: Refunds an amount from one chosen transaction without lines, with a reason and optional reason reference.
nodes.detail: OrderManualTransactionRefundForm validates with a Zod schema that the amount is positive and not above the chosen transaction's charged amount, and calls transactionRequestAction with action REFUND, then returns to the order.

nodes.name: Legacy payment refund view
nodes.summary: Refunds orders on the older payments model, either a miscellaneous amount or specific fulfilled and unfulfilled products.
nodes.detail: A miscellaneous refund calls orderRefund with an amount; a products refund calls orderFulfillmentRefundProducts with order lines, fulfilment lines, shipping and an optional amount.

nodes.name: Reason reference picker
nodes.summary: Picks a model (a content page of the configured page type) as the reason reference for a refund or return.

nodes.name: Returns
nodes.summary: Returning or replacing fulfilled, waiting and unfulfilled items, with an optional granted refund and automatic send in the same submit.
nodes.detail: OrderReturn runs orderFulfillmentReturnProducts first. If that succeeds and staff ticked 'grant refund', useRefundWithinReturn creates a granted refund and, with 'send refund', immediately requests it through the first transaction. Orders on the legacy payments model refund inside the return mutation itself.

nodes.name: Return order view
nodes.summary: Submits the return, then the optional grant and send refund, shows one result toast and navigates back to the order.
nodes.detail: A replacement creates a new order; onCompleted stores its identifier in state for the final navigation. CANNOT_REFUND errors get a dedicated toast. The page shows order data from the latest mutation response if any.

nodes.name: useRefundWithinReturn()
nodes.summary: Creates a granted refund for the returned lines and optionally sends it, returning both error lists.
nodes.detail: prepareGrantRefundLines maps fulfilment line rows to their order line identifiers and squashLines adds up quantities per order line, because the grant refund mutation takes order lines only.

nodes.name: Return input parser
nodes.summary: ReturnFormDataParser turns the return form into OrderReturnProductsInput: fulfilment and order lines with quantity, replace flag and reasons.
nodes.detail: Waiting-for-approval lines are sent as fulfilment lines. With refunds enabled (legacy payments) it adds the amount to refund (manual mode only), shipping and a refund flag that is true when any returned line is not replaced; with transactions it sends amount 0 and refund false.

nodes.name: Return page
nodes.summary: Return form with item cards per fulfilment, return reasons, replace switches, and the refund or transaction submit card.
nodes.detail: form.tsx holds formsets for fulfilled, waiting and unfulfilled quantities, items to replace and line reasons. TransactionSubmitCard offers grant refund, send refund, refund shipping and transaction selection; PaymentSubmitCard is the legacy refund amount card.

nodes.name: Order, refund and return settings
nodes.summary: Shop-wide and per-channel order settings, and the refund and return reason settings.
nodes.detail: Order settings saves shop settings (fulfilment auto-approve, allow unpaid, stock reservation, checkout quantity limit) with shopSettingsUpdate and each changed channel's order settings with channelUpdate, in parallel, skipping parts the user has no permission for. Refunds settings (src/refundsSettings) chooses the model type that refund and return reasons must reference.

nodes.name: Order settings view
nodes.summary: Loads shop and channel order settings and saves them through submitOrderSettingsForm.

nodes.name: submitOrderSettingsForm()
nodes.summary: Sends the shop settings update and one channelUpdate per changed channel in parallel and collects errors per channel.
nodes.detail: Skips the shop update when nothing changed or the user lacks MANAGE_SETTINGS, and channel updates when the user cannot update channels. Returns failed channel identifiers so the page can keep those rows dirty.

nodes.name: Refunds and returns settings view
nodes.summary: Chooses the model type refund and return reasons must reference, or clears it, and previews models of that type.
nodes.detail: Runs RefundSettings, ReturnSettings and ModelTypes; saving calls refundSettingsUpdate and returnSettingsUpdate, or the reference clear mutations when the type is removed.

nodes.name: Refund settings GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Queries for refund settings, return settings and model types, and mutations to update or clear their reason reference type.
nodes.detail: The reason reference type is a model (page) type; once set, refund and return reasons must reference a model of that type. Removing the type runs the dedicated reference clear mutations.

nodes.name: Customer GraphQL queries
nodes.summary: Customer list, customer details (with orders and key figures by channel), addresses, type attributes and create data.
nodes.detail: CustomerDetails takes permission flags so orders and private metadata are only requested for staff who may see them, a key figures channel and a switch for the order count. kpiOrderChannels reads up to 50 orders to learn which channels the customer used.

nodes.name: Customer GraphQL mutations
nodes.summary: Create, update, delete and bulk delete customers, and create, update, delete and set default addresses.
nodes.detail: Each mutation selects its account errors; customerUpdate also returns the CustomerDetails fragment so the cached customer refreshes, and address mutations return the user with the CustomerAddresses fragment.

nodes.name: Customer list view
nodes.summary: Lists customers with filters, search, sort, customer type tabs with counts, and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: useCustomerTypeTabCounts runs one page-size ListCustomers query per type tab (so a count can read as 'more'); bulk delete calls customerBulkDelete and refetches.

nodes.name: CustomerDetailsProvider
nodes.summary: Loads the customer twice: once to find channels with orders, then scoped to the selected channel for key figures.
nodes.detail: The scoped query is skipped without MANAGE_ORDERS or before a channel is known; the first channel found becomes the default. Refetch reloads both and is registered for app-triggered refreshes.

nodes.name: Customer details view
nodes.summary: Saves identity, note, customer type and attributes in one customerUpdate, handles activate, deactivate and delete dialogs.
nodes.detail: New file attribute values are uploaded first; getCustomerUpdateAttributesInput sends only changed attributes, or all of them when the type changed. A type change refetches the customer and resets the attribute form.

nodes.name: Customer details page
nodes.summary: Page with customer info, type and attributes, overview figures, recent orders, addresses, gift cards, external reference and app widgets.
nodes.detail: saveComposition.ts records which parts (general, type, attributes) are dirty so the save bar hint can say what will be saved.

nodes.name: Customer attribute helpers
nodes.summary: Maps customer type attributes to form inputs and back to the customerUpdate attributes input.
nodes.detail: useCustomerDetailsAttributes loads the type's attributes (CustomerTypeAttributesForCustomer) when the type changes in the form, so the attribute card can show the new type's fields before saving.

nodes.name: Customer addresses view
nodes.summary: Adds, edits, deletes and sets default shipping or billing addresses for a customer.

nodes.name: Create customer view
nodes.summary: Creates a customer with name, email, note and default address, then opens the new customer.

nodes.name: Customer routes and addresses
nodes.summary: Customer section routes and web address builders, including dialog actions on the details page.
nodes.detail: index.tsx routes /customers/ to the list, /customers/add to creation (guarded by SectionRoute permissions), /customers/:id/addresses to addresses and /customers/:id to details. urls.ts keeps dialog state such as remove, activate and deactivate in the query string.

nodes.name: Customer types
nodes.summary: Customer types: list, create, details with assigned attributes, default type and deletion with an assigned-customers warning.
nodes.detail: Routes in src/customerTypes/index.tsx. Details runs customerTypeUpdate (also for 'set as default'), assign, unassign and reorder attribute mutations, and can create a customer attribute in place and assign it. Deleting first counts customers of that type.

nodes.name: Customer type details view
nodes.summary: Edits a customer type's name, default flag, attributes (assign, create, unassign, reorder) and metadata.

nodes.name: Customer type list view
nodes.summary: Lists customer types with search and sort and opens the create dialog.

nodes.name: Customer type GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Queries for the type list, details and assigned customer count; mutations to create, update, delete and manage attributes.
nodes.detail: CustomerTypeAssignedCustomersCount asks for the number of customers filtered by type, so deletion can warn how many customers lose their type.

nodes.name: Gift card list
nodes.summary: Gift card list page with search and filters, data grid, bulk activate, deactivate and delete, and issue buttons.
nodes.detail: GiftCardListProvider builds GiftCardList variables from filters, sort and pagination; GiftCardListDialogsProvider opens the create, bulk create, delete and save-search dialogs.

nodes.name: Gift card bulk actions
nodes.summary: Activates or deactivates the selected gift cards in one mutation and refetches the list.

nodes.name: Issue gift card dialog
nodes.summary: Issues one gift card with balance, tags, expiry, assigned customer, activation and optional email to a customer, then shows its code.
nodes.detail: Ignores close while the mutation runs, and shows the generated code on success so staff can copy it.

nodes.name: getCreateGiftCardInputData()
nodes.summary: Builds GiftCardCreateInput: email and channel only when sending to a customer, active unless activation is required, expiry from date or period.
nodes.detail: getGiftCardExpiryInputData adds a day, week, month or year period to the current date and formats it as YYYY-MM-DD, or passes the chosen date through.

nodes.name: Bulk issue dialog
nodes.summary: Issues many gift cards with the same balance, tags, expiry and activation, validating the form locally first.
nodes.detail: Sends giftCardBulkCreate with count, balance, tags, expiry and isActive, refetches the list and reports how many cards were created.

nodes.name: Gift card details
nodes.summary: Gift card details page inside the details, update form and dialogs providers: balance, customer, provenance, history and metadata.
nodes.detail: GiftCardDetailsProvider runs GiftCardDetails; GiftCardUpdateFormProvider saves tags (as added and removed lists) and the expiry date with giftCardUpdate; saveComposition.ts records which parts changed for the save bar hint.

nodes.name: Activate and deactivate toggle
nodes.summary: Activates or deactivates the gift card from the page header and shows a toast.

nodes.name: Resend code dialog
nodes.summary: Resends the gift card code by email in a chosen channel, to the last recipient by default or to another address.
nodes.detail: getGiftCardResendDefaultRecipient offers no default once the card was used (the server then resends to the last user), otherwise the email of the latest SENT_TO_CUSTOMER or RESENT event, otherwise the creator.

nodes.name: Balance, customer and note dialogs
nodes.summary: Changes the balance (through giftCardUpdate), assigns or unassigns a customer, and adds timeline notes.

nodes.name: Gift card settings
nodes.summary: Sets the default expiry for new gift cards (never or a time period) with giftCardSettingsUpdate.

nodes.name: Customer gift cards card
nodes.summary: Card on the customer page listing gift cards used by the customer, with an issue button.

nodes.name: Promotions
nodes.summary: Promotion list, create page and details page, with name, description, dates and a list of rules.
nodes.detail: Create sends the whole promotion with its rules in one promotionCreate. Details saves the general form with promotionUpdate and each rule separately with promotionRuleCreate, promotionRuleUpdate or promotionRuleDelete from the rule modal. Because the server validates dates against the stored end date, clearing the end date while moving the start past it is done in two updates.

nodes.name: Discount GraphQL queries
nodes.summary: Queries for promotions, vouchers, voucher catalogue, assigned identifiers, codes, rule option labels and gift labels.
nodes.detail: Also holds plain query strings for the developer GraphQL playground (PromotionDetailsQuery and the GraphiQL voucher and promotion queries). SaleList is still used by the dry-run items list; SaleDetails has no caller.

nodes.name: Discount GraphQL mutations
nodes.summary: Mutations for vouchers (create, update, delete, catalogues, channel listings, codes) and promotions and their rules.
nodes.detail: Voucher catalogue mutations take pagination and include flags so the response can refresh the visible catalogue tab. The promotion rule create document is exported as promotinRuleCreate (a misspelt constant name).

nodes.name: Promotion list view
nodes.summary: Lists promotions with conditional filters, search, sort and presets.

nodes.name: Create promotion view
nodes.summary: Creates a promotion of type catalogue or order with dates and rules in one promotionCreate, then opens it.
nodes.detail: useDiscountCreate converts each rule with toAPI(type), parses the rich text description and joins date and time.

nodes.name: Promotion details view
nodes.summary: Loads a promotion, its condition labels and gift labels, and wires update, delete and rule create, update and delete.
nodes.detail: usePromotionData runs PromotionDetails; useFetchConditionsOptionsDetails resolves product, variant, category and collection names for the rules' conditions.

nodes.name: createUpdateHandler() (promotion)
nodes.summary: Updates a promotion, first clearing its end date in a separate silent update when the new start would pass it, and restoring it on failure.
nodes.detail: shouldClearPromotionEndDateFirst is true when the end date is being removed and the new start is after the stored end. If the main update fails or throws, the cleared end date is put back so the promotion does not run open-ended.

nodes.name: Promotion rules and conditions
nodes.summary: The rule list and rule modal (channel, conditions, reward) and the models that translate rules to and from server predicates.
nodes.detail: A Rule has a channel, conditions (product, variant, category, collection, or for order promotions base subtotal and base total price), a reward value type (percentage or fixed) and value, and for order promotions a reward type (subtotal discount or gifts). Catalogue rules become a cataloguePredicate with one '<kind>Predicate' entry per condition, joined with OR when there are several; order rules become an orderPredicate with a discountedObjectPredicate. Predicates with nested conditions the form cannot show are left untouched.

nodes.name: toAPI() and mapAPIRuleToForm()
nodes.summary: Converts a form Rule to PromotionRuleInput (predicate and reward by promotion type) and a server rule back to a form Rule.
nodes.detail: Order promotions with a GIFT reward send gifts and null reward values; catalogue promotions never send a reward type. Predicates are cast from untyped JavaScript Object Notation (JSON); the code notes a parsing schema is still missing.

nodes.name: prepareCataloguePredicate()
nodes.summary: Builds a catalogue predicate from conditions, skipping empty ones and joining several with OR.

nodes.name: prepareOrderPredicate()
nodes.summary: Builds an order predicate's discountedObjectPredicate from subtotal or total conditions, joined with OR.
nodes.detail: createAPIWhereInput turns an operator (is, lower, greater, between) and value into a decimal filter input.

nodes.name: Rule and Condition models
nodes.summary: Form-side types and defaults for rules and conditions, and the reverse parsers from server predicates.
nodes.detail: prepareCatalogueRuleConditions reads '<kind>Predicate' keys back into conditions with labels from the options lookup; prepareOrderConditions reads subtotal and total filters back into operator and value.

nodes.name: Rules list and modal
nodes.summary: Shows rule summaries and opens the rule form modal to add, edit or delete a rule, with a link to the GraphQL playground.
nodes.detail: RuleFormModal validates with a Zod schema (validationSchema.ts); RuleForm renders channel, conditions, reward type and value. useGraphQLPlayground opens the developer panel preloaded with the promotion query.

nodes.name: Vouchers and codes
nodes.summary: Voucher list, create and details pages: discount type and values per channel, requirements, limits, countries, catalogue scope and codes.
nodes.detail: Voucher details keeps catalogue additions and removals, country changes and code deletions as a local draft. On save it runs voucherUpdate first (details, countries, new codes), then channel listings, code deletions and catalogue changes in parallel, and reports which parts were saved. If channel values for a new discount type are rejected, it reverts the type so saved amounts do not change meaning.

nodes.name: Voucher list view
nodes.summary: Lists vouchers with filters, search, sort and presets, and deletes selected vouchers in bulk.

nodes.name: Create voucher view
nodes.summary: Creates a voucher, then sets its channel listings; deletes the new voucher again if the channel step fails.
nodes.detail: createHandler in handlers.ts validates the form, sends voucherCreate (codes, type, value type, requirements, limits, dates and catalogue) and then voucherChannelListingUpdate. When the channel step fails it deletes the new voucher (NOT_FOUND counts as deleted) and, if that delete fails too, reports the identifier of the voucher left without channels.

nodes.name: Voucher details view
nodes.summary: Loads a voucher, its catalogue and codes, stages catalogue and code changes, and saves everything through createUpdateHandler.
nodes.detail: useVoucherCatalogueDraft holds staged catalogue changes; useVoucherCodes combines server codes with new local codes and row selection.

nodes.name: createUpdateHandler() (voucher)
nodes.summary: Saves voucher details first, then channels, code deletions and catalogue changes in parallel, returning errors and saved parts.
nodes.detail: Stops after a failed details update. Code deletion errors are relabelled to the codes field so the save failure toast scrolls to the codes section.

nodes.name: Voucher catalogue draft
nodes.summary: Pure functions that stage catalogue additions and removals and turn them into add and remove catalogue inputs.
nodes.detail: Each catalogue kind (categories, collections, products, variants) has a bucket of added and removed items; staging an add cancels a pending remove of the same item and the reverse. The draft also tracks country codes.

nodes.name: Voucher codes
nodes.summary: Codes card with a data grid, manual and generated code dialogs and code deletion.
nodes.detail: Generated codes use a prefix and a quantity; new codes are sent as addCodes in voucherUpdate.

nodes.name: Voucher status and validation
nodes.summary: Voucher status (scheduled, active, finished, used up), value and minimum spend validation, and save error mapping.
nodes.detail: getVoucherStatus compares dates with now and the usage limit with used count; voucherValueValidation checks percentage and fixed values and whole-number fields; getVoucherSaveRequestErrors turns a failed request into one error so callers handle request failures and payload errors the same way.

nodes.name: Discount routes and addresses
nodes.summary: Discount section routes and web address builders; promotions keep the legacy sales paths.
nodes.detail: Promotions live at /discounts/sales/, /discounts/sales/add and /discounts/sales/:id; vouchers at /discounts/vouchers/, /discounts/vouchers/add and /discounts/vouchers/:id.

nodes.name: Granted refund helpers
nodes.summary: Finds order-level granted refunds (no lines) that are drafts or failed, and computes line amounts and failure messages.
nodes.detail: getOrderLevelGrantedRefundsNeedingAttention feeds the refund callout above the order lines; getGrantedRefundLineAmount prices one line of a granted refund; getGrantedRefundFailureMessage reads the failure reason from the transaction events.

nodes.name: Delivery and discount labels
nodes.summary: Describes the delivery method (shipping method or warehouse pickup) and groups discount types for display.
nodes.detail: getDeliveryMethodInfo labels a Warehouse delivery method as pickup and anything else as shipping; getDiscountTypeCategory folds order discount types into manual, voucher, promotion (including order promotions and legacy sales) or other.

nodes.name: useCaptureState()
nodes.summary: Computes authorized, charged and remaining amounts for the capture dialog and the default amount to capture.

nodes.name: grantRefundReducer()
nodes.summary: Reducer for the older grant refund page: per-line selected quantities, shipping and a custom amount.

nodes.name: Customer key figures
nodes.summary: Computes a customer's recent net sales, average order value, shipping and refunded totals in one channel.
nodes.detail: Uses the last 10 placed orders in the chosen channel, excluding drafts and cancelled orders. extractChannelsFromOrders orders channels by the customer's most recent qualifying order, which picks the default channel for the overview.

nodes.name: Customer feature announcements
nodes.summary: Ripple entries announcing the customer overview and the new customers view.

nodes.name: Gift card list state
nodes.summary: Context provider holding the gift card list's filters, sort, pagination, selection and query result.

nodes.name: Gift card delete
nodes.summary: Delete dialogs for one gift card (details page) or the selected cards (list), with single and bulk delete hooks.

nodes.name: Gift card permissions
nodes.summary: Tells gift card screens whether the user can manage gift cards and channels and see users, staff creators and apps.

nodes.name: createHandler() (voucher create)
nodes.summary: Creates the voucher, saves channel values, and deletes the voucher again when the channel step is rejected.

nodes.name: Voucher form handlers
nodes.summary: Form change handlers for voucher scope, discount type and channels, and the channel listing input builder.
nodes.detail: getChannelsVariables builds voucherChannelListingUpdate input: channels to add with discount value and minimum spend, and channels to remove. createVoucherScopeChangeHandler sets the shipping type for free shipping and, when leaving it, resets the discount to percentage and clears the shipping channel amounts.

nodes.name: Voucher discount and scope section
nodes.summary: Chooses the voucher's discount type and scope (entire order, specific products, shipping) and its value per channel.

nodes.name: Rule summaries
nodes.summary: Lists a promotion's rules as readable summaries (channel, conditions, reward) with edit and delete actions.

nodes.name: Promotion rule hooks
nodes.summary: Hooks that run promotionRuleCreate, promotionRuleUpdate and promotionRuleDelete, write the change into the cached promotion and show a toast.

flows.name: A staff member fulfils an order
flows.summary: From the order details page to a created fulfilment, including the stock-exceeded retry and approval.

steps.text: A staff member opens an order and clicks Fulfill on the unfulfilled lines (or on one line from the line matrix).
The placed order sub-view navigates to /orders/:id/fulfill, optionally with a lineId parameter.
The fulfil view runs OrderFulfillData for the lines and stocks and OrderFulfillSettings for the shop's auto-approve and allow-unpaid flags.
Each line still to fulfil is prefilled with its full quantity and the warehouse holding its biggest allocation, or the most available stock.
Staff adjust quantities and warehouses and add a tracking number. Save stays disabled while a line is over-fulfilled, lacks a warehouse, or the shop forbids fulfilling unpaid orders.
On save the formset becomes FulfillOrder lines, dropping zero quantities and rows without a warehouse.
The dashboard sends the FulfillOrder mutation to the GraphQL endpoint.
Core validates stock and creates the fulfilments, which wait for approval unless the shop auto-approves them.
If every error is INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, the stock-exceeded dialog lists the short lines and lets staff resubmit with allowStockToBeExceeded.
On success it replaces the history entry with the order page and shows 'Fulfilled Items'.
A fulfilment waiting for approval is approved from its card, which runs orderFulfillmentApprove and can notify the customer.

flows.name: A staff member grants and sends a refund
flows.summary: Creating a refund draft from order lines, then transferring the funds through the payment app and watching the result arrive.

steps.text: On a placed order, staff click to add a refund in the refunds table above the transactions.
The dialog asks for a standard refund (with lines) or a manual refund; manual needs the HANDLE_PAYMENTS permission.
The create page loads OrderDetailsGrantRefund and the refund settings that say which model a refund reason must reference.
Staff pick lines and quantities, shipping, the transaction and a reason; the amount follows the selection unless edited.
An amount above the chosen transaction's charged amount is rejected locally; otherwise lines with a positive quantity are mapped to order line identifiers.
Save draft sends OrderGrantRefundAdd.
Core stores the granted refund with status NONE (a draft) and returns its identifier.
The dashboard opens the draft's edit page. With a clean form and HANDLE_PAYMENTS, the save bar now offers Transfer funds.
getRefundFormSubmitBehavior switches the submit action from saving the draft to transferring funds.
Transfer sends transactionRequestRefundForGrantedRefund for the draft and its transaction.
Core checks the refund is not pending or done and fits the charged amount, records a REFUND_REQUEST event and asks the payment app to refund.
The transaction-refund-requested event goes to the app that owns the transaction as a synchronous webhook.
Back on the order, the unresolved request turns on polling every 5 seconds until a success or failure event arrives, for up to 24 cycles.
The refunds table then shows the refund as successful or failed, with the failure message from the app.

flows.name: A staff member creates a promotion with rules
flows.summary: From the promotion form to promotionCreate with predicates built from the rule conditions.

steps.text: Staff open Discounts, add a promotion, choose catalogue or order type, name, description and dates.
Each rule is edited in the rule modal: channel, conditions such as products or categories (or subtotal for order promotions), and the reward.
On save each form rule is converted to PromotionRuleInput for the chosen promotion type.
Catalogue conditions become '<kind>Predicate' entries with identifiers, joined with OR when there are several.
promotionCreate stores the promotion with its rules; the dashboard then opens the details page, where later rule edits run one rule mutation each.
